title: Theater pit versus dance band with Blossom Seeley
summary: He learned from the piano with Seeley's act and contrasts hearing each other in a band with the spread-out pit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Just like when with Celie now. She had a colored boy around New York by the name of Bill Beaudry. Bill Beaudry made all her arrangements. He made arrangements for the Ziegfeld, see? And the Dillingham shows. Bill Beaudry made her arrangements for her act. Other than the popular songs that were my act, I had to do what I want with them. But the big introductions and the finales and stuff like that. Yeah. And I sat right there. Of course we played, I learned mine from the piano, see? Charlie played the piano and I'd sit on the alongside and get a load of it. But when you sit in an orchestra pit, it's not sitting in a band. No. You sit in a band, you know, the drums are behind you here on this side and the bass is over here, you know, and the piano's here and you droop around this way and you can hear each other. But you get in a theater pit, that's all lost. Spreads out. The drums were on this end and the bass were on that end and the violins are over there and you don't hear what the clarinet and the flute are playing.
And the trombone and the trumpet, they sit here and you don't hear nothing. In an orchestra or a dance band, you hear everything.
